baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core facts (2500 g martensite, 2900 g austenite, 400 g total actuation force, 15-20 C austenite range, 10 g per louver) and both repeat the same fabricated splice quote for the 10 g criterion and the same misread 'Austenite --deformation--> Martensite' transition (the diagram's deformation arrow runs between the two Martensite states). Set A additionally invents a '-200C' lower bound not in the text and loosely binds the 400 g actuation force to the shading mechanism rather than the wire. Set B makes more binding errors around the 10 g figure, calling it 'maximum friction' and attaching it to 'axial rotation points' and to the 'Flexinol actuated shading system' instead of per louver, and adds a further non-verbatim quote. Overall A is somewhat cleaner, though both are heavily duplicated.

variant-first.note: Both sets are heavily duplicated and share the same core facts (2500 g martensite pull force, 2900 g austenite pull force, 400 g total actuation force, 10 g max pull force per louver, 15–20C austenite range) and the same misread of the diagram (claiming an Austenite→Martensite deformation arrow that does not exist). Set A additionally captures the transformation temperature range correctly (200C to cryogenic, by Ni:Ti ratio) with a supporting quote, whereas Set B only states it reversed and once invents a '-200C' endpoint not in the source. Set A's clear errors are binding 10 grams to 'maximum friction' at the axial rotation points and to the shading system rather than the louver; Set B misbinds the 400 g total actuation force to the shading mechanism and fabricates the -200C value. On balance A covers the key temperature fact faithfully while B omits it, so A is slightly better.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds the state-space matrices correctly (A_d=α, B_d=1−α, C_d=α, D_d=1−α as the input transmission matrix) and gives plot readings with quotes that actually reference the plotted values (e.g., magnitude ≈ −12.5 dB at 1.00 Hz). Set B repeatedly uses the figure caption as the quote for Bode-plot values (phase −75°, magnitude −12 dB at 1.00 Hz), so those claims are unsupported, and it adds misread points (phase −30° at 0.10 Hz, −75° at 0.5 Hz) plus a garbled property name ('input mission matrix' for the input transmission matrix). Both sets contain duplicates and one claim each that contradicts its own quote (−80° vs. −75 at 1.00 Hz), and both approximate the −3 dB point as ≈0.2–0.3 Hz instead of the stated 0.25 Hz. Overall A keeps the needed conditions and correct bindings more consistently, so it is the better set.

variant-first.note: Set A binds all four discrete-time matrices correctly (A_d=α, B_d=1−α, C_d=α, D_d=1−α with the correct 'input transmission matrix' label), states the corner frequency as 0.25 Hz at the −3 dB point tied to one-quarter of the blade's first edgewise natural frequency, and gives consistent Bode reads (0 dB/0° at 0.01 Hz, −12 dB and −75° at 1.00 Hz, −30° at 0.10 Hz). Set B repeats the B_d=1−α claim four times, misbinds D_d to the 'discrete-time input matrix', restates the corner frequency as '0.25 fraction', and alters the quote for the transmission matrix. B also misreads chart values against its own quotes (−80° where its quote says −75, −12.5 dB where its quote says −12) and puts −45° at ≈0.2 Hz although −45° occurs at the 0.25 Hz corner. A's main flaws are one misread (−75° at 0.5 Hz), one claim contradicting its own quote (−80° at 1.00 Hz), and a fabricated quote fragment ('input mission matrix').

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core facts (FIRST FLR 2'-4" above GRADE LEVEL 0", 2" X 8" joist/frame, 3/8" X 4" hex through bolt, 3/4" threaded rod, 1" nut, A6 landscape footing 18"), but Set A makes more misbindings: it assigns the 3/4" X 5 1/2" decking size to the joist, calls the 1" nut a 'nut sleeve', labels the 4X4 post a footing member type, and dumps unrelated 1'-0", 1 1/2" and 7 1/2" dimensions onto 'C1 DECKING' or the landscape footing, plus an invented 'offset from edge to post 1' attribute. Set B keeps the plywood deck and reclaimed wood surface sizes correctly separated, adds the bolt length/head type and plywood thickness, and its errors are mostly dimensions (1 1/4", 3 3/4", 8'-0", 1 1/2") attached to the wrong detail or component. Both sets contain vague 'component 1' entries and duplicates, but Set B is more faithful overall.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the material and member sizes more faithfully: plywood/reclaimed wood surface 3/4" x 5 1/2", 2" x 8" joist and frame, 3/8" x 4" hex through bolt (including head type), 3/4" threaded rod, and the FIRST FLR 2'-4" / GRADE LEVEL 0" elevations all match the B1/B4/C3 callouts. Set B makes clear misbindings and inventions: it assigns 3/4" x 5 1/2" to the joist (with a garbled quote), labels the 4X4 post as a footing member type, invents an 'offset from edge to post 1' attribute, merges '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' into one 'nut sleeve' dimension, and files several A6/C1 dimensions under 'C1 DECKING' or the landscape footing. Both sets have vague 'component 1' claims and misfile some A6 detail dimensions (1 1/4", 3 3/4", 8'-0", 1'-0"), but A's errors are fewer and less severe, and A captures the through-bolt head type and plywood thickness that B misses.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core Nitinol facts (martensite/austenite structures, 4-5% strain, 25,000 PSI force, 2-5% typical contraction, 55-65% Ni / 44-55% Ti) and both repeat the same two fabricated values (hysteresis '20-50C' instead of 25-50C, and '20,000 PSI' instead of 25,000 PSI). Set A adds extra problems: a vague 'Titanium composition: not specified percent' claim, a mislabeled 'strain stress' for the 25,000 PSI force, and it misbinds the 15-30C transition range to the 'Harvest Shade Screen' when the source says 'in the context of the linear diffuser'. Set B keeps that condition correct and its commercial transition claim (90C) is merely incomplete rather than wrong, though it also misquotes 'mechanical stress' for 'mechanical force'. Overall B is the more faithful set despite heavy duplication in both.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the core facts (martensite at low temperature, austenite on heating, 4–5% strain, 2–5% typical contraction, 55–65% Ni / 44–55% Ti) and both repeat the same two errors: a hysteresis range of 20–50 C (source says 25–50C) and a strain force of 20,000 PSI (source says 25,000 PSI). Set A binds the 15–30 C transition temperature to the correct condition (context of the linear diffuser) and gives the 25,000 PSI figure, whereas Set B misbinds that condition to the Harvest Shade Screen and adds a vague 'not specified percent' titanium claim plus a misbound 'during austenite phase' condition. Set A's weaknesses are a garbled quote for the nickel composition, 'mechanical stress' quoted where the source says 'mechanical force', and listing only 90 C for commercially available wire (source gives 70C and 90C). On balance A has fewer misread or misbound claims, though both sets are close.

baseline-first.note: Set A contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the page's stated concerns. Set B provides two claims that are faithful to the text: the HabEx mission scope is described as quite ambitious, and the thermal control requirements are called challenging, with quotes that support each. Set B omits the ATD cost breakout concern, but it still captures substantially more correct content than the empty Set A, with no misread or invented claims.

variant-first.note: Set A captures two of the three overarching concerns on the page with faithful quotes and correct binding (HabEx mission scope ambitious; thermal control requirements challenging). Set B returns no claims at all, so it omits every fact on the page. A's claims are qualitative but accurately reflect the source, and nothing is invented. The ATD cost-breakout concern is missed by both.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain duplicates and vague entities, but Set B correctly binds LUVOIR-A's four science instruments to LUVOIR-A, whereas Set A misbinds that fact to a garbled 'n-axis telescope' and adds two unsupported 'axis telescope' instrument-count claims plus a vague 'baseline mission spacecraft' claim. Set A also misstates the Lynx 10 m focal length as a mirror 'dimension'/'size' twice (Set B does this once) and includes a truncated quote ('52 m starsha'). Set B's remaining weaknesses are the same misbound 10 m dimension, one garbled 'n-axis telescope' claim, and a vague 'spacecraft' instrument count, so it is the more faithful set overall.

variant-first.note: Both sets contain duplicated and generic entities, but Set A binds the key facts more faithfully and includes LUVOIR-A's four science instruments, which Set B omits. Set B adds two garbled 'axis telescope | 3 instruments' claims and two misbound claims that call Lynx's 10 m focal length a 'dimension'/'size', plus a truncated 'starsha' quote. Set A's main flaws are one garbled 'n-axis telescope' claim, one misbound 10 m 'dimension' claim, and a vague 'spacecraft' instrument-count claim.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the ~100 issues and concerns from the initial LCIT reviews across the four mission concepts. Both then add two redundant, misbound claims: the value 100 is attributed to mission concepts (claim 3 in both), when the text says there are four mission concepts and 100 issues/concerns. Set A's second claim is worse — it binds 100 to a 'resultant mission concepts count' and uses a stitched, non-contiguous quote — whereas Set B's second claim at least keeps a contiguous quote, though it still misattributes 100 to findings of the Draft Final Reports rather than issues raised by the reviews.

variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the ~100 issues and concerns from initial LCIT reviews across the four mission concepts. Set A's second claim at least loosely ties the 100 findings to the Draft Final Reports, whereas Set B's second claim invents a 'resultant mission concepts count' of 100, which contradicts the text (there are four mission concepts). Both sets share the same third claim that misbinds 100 to 'mission concepts quantity' instead of issues and concerns. Set A is marginally better due to one less egregiously misbound claim.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core datum and scale facts (grade level 0'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", and the 3/8" = 1'-0" scales for sections C1 and A1) with supporting quotes. Set B additionally extracts the revision table entries (marks 1-5 with dates and descriptions), the project name, and the lot number, all of which are clearly supported by the text layer and title block. Set A omits these important title-block and revision facts and instead repeats the grade level and finished floor values several times in near-identical claims, adding no new information. Neither set contains a clearly misread or invented value, so B wins on coverage and faithfulness.

variant-first.note: Set A captures the full revision history (marks 1–5 with dates and descriptions), the lot number (116), and the section scales, all supported by the title block and section labels; Set B omits all of these, which counts against it. Both sets contain redundant repeats of the grade level and finished floor elevations, and both bind the elevation markers to the correct sections. Set A's only questionable claim is labeling the client block text as the project name, a minor misbinding; otherwise its added claims are faithful.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the two annotated Figure 7-3 values (∂P/∂θ at θ=0 = -25.52E+6 watt/rad and θK = 6.302336°) and the doubling relation, but both are padded with heavy duplication and several unsupported graph reads. Set A includes a clearly wrong read (-90E+6 at the last data point, which is about -120E+6) plus two -30E+6 claims at θ=0 that contradict the annotated -25.52E+6, and it states the doubling relation with the wrong condition ('at rated operating point' instead of at θK). Set B has one wrong read (-105E+6 at the maximum plotted pitch angle) and one rough read (-110E+6 at 20°), but its θ=0 read (-25E+6) is consistent with the annotation, its relation claim carries the correct condition, and it adds the supported fact that the pitch-sensitivity/blade-pitch relation is linear in Region 3.

variant-first.note: Both sets are heavily duplicative and share the same misbinding of pitch sensitivity to a 'Blade-Pitch Controller' entity, but A keeps the key definitional facts better: it states the doubling relation with the correct condition (at θK) and includes the linear pitch-sensitivity/blade-pitch relation, whereas B labels the doubling relation 'at rated operating point' and twice truncates the quote to '∂θ (θ =0º) = ...'. B also misbinds pitch sensitivity and θK to 'Rotor-Collective Blade-Pitch' and gives a clearly wrong -90E+6 watt/rad at the last data point (the plot shows about -120E+6 there). A's weak points are unsupported chart-read estimates (-105E+6 at max pitch angle, -30E+6 at 0º, -110E+6 at 20º, -25E+6 at 0º) whose quotes are only axis or legend labels.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are heavily redundant, repeating the same equations (7-6) through (7-10) many times, and both correctly capture the T_Gen and T_Aero expressions and their Taylor expansions. Set A's only defect is one PID-law claim whose derivative term drops the ΔΩ̇ dot (rendered as K_D N_Gear ΔΩ); Set B repeats that same error and additionally misreads the PID gains as K_{P N_Gear}, K_{I N_Gear}, K_{D N_Gear} instead of K_P N_Gear, K_I N_Gear, K_D N_Gear. Set B uniquely captures the constant-generator-power statement in Region 3, while Set A uniquely captures the negligible-variation-of-aerodynamic-torque assumption, so coverage is close, but Set B has one more misread formula.

variant-first.note: Both sets are heavily redundant, restating the same four or five equations many times, but Set A's restatements are mostly faithful to Eqs. (7-6) through (7-10), keeping the Region 3 and negligible-rotor-speed-variation conditions and the full-span blade-pitch definition. Set B introduces more defects: a garbled entity ('Gen 2 Gear'), several quotes with mangled LaTeX ('rac{...}'), truncated quotes ('on 3 is inversely proportional...'), quotes altered with bracketed insertions ('the [torque]'), a PID variant that drops the integral sign, and a vague 'negligible variation' claim. Set A's main errors are one PID rendering that misbinds the gains as K_{P N_Gear} etc. and one that drops the dot on the derivative term; Set B repeats the dot-dropping error and adds roughly half a dozen further misread or unsupported items.

Set B invents or misreads several airfoil names ("FFA-W3-3", "FFA-W3-2", "SNL-FFA") and binds axis-tick values (1.0, 0.0, -1.0, 20, 15) to them as if they were curve data, producing about a dozen unsupported claims. Set A keeps the correct legend entities and Reynolds numbers and gives plausible curve readings (e.g., FFA-W3-211 max cl/cd ~120, FFA-W3-360 max cl/cd ~75). A does contain a few internally inconsistent or overstated values (SNL-FFA-W3-500 max cl/cd 110 and cd 0.08 at cl=1.5, FFA-W3-360 max cl/cd 95, cl=2.0 at 20 deg), and some quotes only cite legend text rather than the plotted value. Overall A is clearly the more faithful set.

baseline-first.note: Set A contains several clearly misbound or garbled claims — 'Siding | dimension | 2x4 | CED', 'exterior elevation | material | 2x4 CED', and 'roof/overhang | component | PV SOLAR ARRAY' all misread the 2x4 cedar handrail note and misplace the PV array — plus a truncated quote and a misquoted grade value. Set B is largely faithful, capturing the APSE-20 tube model/quantity, railing post typical condition, door tilt-and-turn operation and the A-511 Hardie reference, with only the PV array 'between grid lines 4 and 6' location unsupported by its quote. B does omit the finished-floor elevation and revision dates that A captures, and both sets contain redundant duplicates, but B has materially fewer wrong claims.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the solar thermal tube model (APSE-20, 2 x, 40 tubes), the door tilt-and-turn note, the A-511 Hardie reference, and the window/door tag numbers correctly, with only one unsupported claim (PV array location 'between grid lines 4 and 6', not stated in the quote). Set B has three clearly misbound claims: 'Siding | dimension | 2x4' and 'exterior elevation | material | 2x4 CED' (2x4 belongs to the cedar handrail, and the quote is a truncated fragment), and 'roof/overhang | component | PV SOLAR ARRAY' (the PV array is not identified as a roof/overhang component). B also duplicates finished-floor and railing-post claims and omits the sheet notes A captured. A's weaknesses are mostly redundancy (repeated solar envelope, grade level, railing post, tube model claims) rather than error.

Both sets contain many vague, unbound claims (e.g., "component | height | 2\"") and repeat values, but Set A binds more values correctly: the drawing scale (1 1/2" = 1'-0"), the L3X3X1/4 angle profile to the PV structural members, the 2'-3 7/8" and 3'-1 5/16" segment lengths, 12'-3 3/4" and 7'-0" overall dimensions, and the C1/S-301 reference. Set B invents bindings such as "web thickness 5/8\"" (the members are L3x3x1/4 angles), "base block spacing" for 4 3/4" and 4 13/16", and misreads a dimension as "4 13", plus it duplicates 6 13/16" and 1'-11 1/8" under conflicting attributes. Set B does capture the 10'-3 3/4" total length of Module B and the 2'-11 7/8" right segment of Module A, which Set A misses, but overall Set A has fewer misbound and invented claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are heavy on bare dimension strings, but Set B binds more values correctly to identifiable parts: the Module A/B segment lengths with left/right conditions (2'-3 7/8" leftmost, 2'-11 7/8"/3'-1 5/16" segments), the L3X3X1/4 angle member profile, and the 1 1/2" = 1'-0" detail scale, all of which the text layer supports. Set A never captures the L3X3X1/4 member profile or the scale, garbles one value into '4 13', and invents properties such as 'web thickness 5/8"' and 'total height from base'. Set B's weakness is invented bindings/conditions (I-beam height, base-block hole/bottom offsets, base-plate offset to center, middle-section height), so it is not clean, but its core claims are better bound and it recovers the key member-size fact.
